input.quote: This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
input.rationale: Our side of the bargain already sits at or above the fallback: Section 14 (p0079) lets Client terminate at will on written notice, with service (and fees) running only to the last day of the following month and no early-termination fee or penalty of any kind, which beats the fallback's 60-90 days' notice and 3-month fee cap (we note the absence of a preferred-position pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, but fees are invoiced monthly in arrears under Section 5, so there is no material prepayment exposure). The failure is on TrueLink's side: its only convenience exit is non-renewal at the end of a one-year term, but on just thirty (30) days' notice, which is below the fallback's 90-day floor and squarely within walk-away territory ("Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice") for a hosting dependency. The single edit extends TrueLink's non-renewal notice to ninety (90) days while preserving our 30-day notice, curing the fallback on its material terms.

proposal.summary: Require TrueLink to give 90 days' notice of non-renewal (its only convenience exit), leaving Client's 30-day notice unchanged.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that a host may only exit at the end of a term and on at least 90 days' notice, so we have extended TrueLink's non-renewal notice to ninety (90) days while leaving our own 30-day notice unchanged.

ops.newText: Client delivers written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days, or TrueLink delivers such notice no later than ninety (90) days, prior to the end of said year
